name: Vishay Precision Group
note: Analyst target nearly doubled to $77 from $39 after a formal vendor nomination letter from an unnamed humanoid robotics developer — a concrete signal, not just narrative. Shares have actually pulled back ~11% over the past month to $60.49, widening the gap. Weight increased on the strength of the nomination letter, funded by trimming Kratos.

name: Johnson & Johnson
note: Ottava's FDA de novo authorization (10 general surgery procedures, granted Jul 22) got a fresh CNBC profile this week (Sep 11) describing a table-integrated design that takes 30-50% less space than cart-based systems like da Vinci — a real competitive signal for surgical robotics. But robotics is a rounding error inside a $450B+ diversified healthcare conglomerate; added to track the Ottava-vs-da Vinci dynamic, not for JNJ's own exposure.

name: BAE Systems
note: The ~11% recovery to ~2,043p this week reaffirms the record £84.0B H1 order backlog and raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales, 11-13% EPS growth) as the least-disputed thesis in the sector; weight raised on the price confirmation. Directly accessible from the UK with no wrapper needed — the most straightforward core holding on this page.

name: AeroVironment
note: The $464.8M Army LOCUST X3 laser award — the Pentagon's first-ever directed-energy production contract — diversifies AeroVironment's revenue beyond the drone segment and lands on top of a record $1.5B backlog; weight raised meaningfully, though the SCAR/BADGER securities-fraud litigation keeps this speculative rather than core. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

name: Kratos Defense
note: Three sell-side targets and a Q2 beat-and-raise still support the CCA-engine optionality (GEK800 testing toward $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue), but Kratos again failed to place on the Sep 18 Gauntlet II leaderboard despite qualifying for both rounds — real evidence against the near-term autonomy-optionality case, so weight trimmed. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

name: Red Cat Holdings
note: Teal Drones missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Close Quarters Battle category, the second straight negative data point after August's insider selling; moving this to Avoid until the maritime-autonomy and swarm-robotics story converts into contracted revenue rather than platform narrative.

name: Centrus Energy
note: The Sep 17 multi-year HALEU supply deal with Antares Nuclear — with customer prepayments funding further Piketon capacity — is the first dated commercial contract behind the DOE build-out, not just a policy tailwind, and shares rose 6.6% on it. Moving off Watch into a small Speculative position on that concrete catalyst.

name: Energy Fuels
note: White Mesa's heavy-rare-earth construction keeps advancing toward 2027 commercial light/heavy REE output, pilot Dy oxide already exceeds automotive spec purity, and the Vacuumschmelze deal remains on track for a Q1 2027 close. No negative catalysts this week — bumping weight slightly to reflect steady execution.

name: Rocket Lab
note: Fully funded its Iridium acquisition on Sept 15 — completing a $1.94B ATM offering and canceling the $3.6B bridge facility — resolving the financing-risk bear case while Craig-Hallum initiated at Buy and Electron flew its 96th mission (17th of 2026) on Sept 19; raising weight as the deal de-risks even though Neutron still isn't flying before 2027.

name: L3Harris
note: Guggenheim initiated coverage Sept 15 at Buy with 49% upside and Space & Mission Systems revenue is tracking to top $13B in 2026, but shares are still hovering near 52-week lows around $250 with the Kubasik-era securities investigation unresolved; raising weight modestly as new analyst conviction argues the backlog isn't being credited. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

name: Redwire
note: Shares fell 7% on Sept 18 even as BofA raised its target to $8 (still Underperform), and a fresh disclosure shows $1.15B of net insider selling over the past 12 months — a scale that dwarfs the roughly $1B market cap and is hard to square with the 'consistent execution' thesis; cutting weight sharply pending clarity on what's driving that selling.

name: AST SpaceMobile
note: BlueBird 12/13 are fully deployed and US Mobile is lining up a Q4 direct-to-cell launch alongside a new Vodafone Ukraine gateway JV, yet shares fell 10% on the news — a sell-the-news reaction that looks more like market noise than a thesis break; nudging weight up as commercial integration keeps advancing.

name: Intuitive Machines
note: Completed the SXM-11 satellite handover Sept 15 and carries a record $1.8B backlog, but shares stayed volatile (+6.6% then -5.9% in consecutive sessions) and insider selling remains heavy ($259.4M net over 12 months); raising size modestly but keeping it small given that selling pattern.

name: Planet Labs
note: Shares are down 67% from their May peak on a proposed $1.5B equity dilution plan, and the CEO sold $2.2M of stock Sept 15 (scheduled tax-withholding, not open-market conviction selling, but it adds to the overhang); staying on Watch until the dilution terms and next guide are clearer.

name: Eos Energy
note: Raised a point, funded by trimming NRGV below: the Google/MN8 deal firmed up to a specific 10MW/100MWh contract and an $87M DOE loan advance is now funding the Thorn Hill second line — real de-risking events, not just sentiment, even though storage revenue on this deal still doesn't start until 2028–2030 and the securities-law investigations remain open.

name: Illumina
note: Officially rejoins the S&P 500 today on a genuine earnings turnaround (FY2025 net income $850M) plus a Sept 9 UBS upgrade to Buy (PT $260, from $135) — fresh 52-week high $239.55, +143% trailing 12mo. Weight increased again on a real fundamental-and-flow catalyst, not just index mechanics.

name: Intellia Therapeutics
note: Now has a firm PDUFA date (March 10, 2027) for lonvo-z plus HAELO Phase 3 data showing an 87% attack-rate reduction and a new $400M credit facility to fund launch — real, continued de-risking. Still pre-approval so stays Speculative, but weight increased again to reflect the improved odds.

name: Quantum-Si
note: Demonstrated detection of 18 of 20 amino acids on Proteus (Sept 15) — the first genuine technical proof point this platform has delivered in months, even with the commercial launch still a confirmed year late (Q2 2027). Upgraded from Avoid on real progress, kept small given the execution history.

name: IBM
note: The single biggest quantum catalyst of the month: Anderon finalized a $1B CHIPS Act award (Sep 16) for its Albany 300mm quantum wafer foundry, matched by another $1B from IBM itself. Nudged up on the scale and specificity of that commitment; still a rounding error on a profitable, dividend-paying business.

name: Alphabet
note: A fifth straight quiet week for Willow-specific hardware milestones; the UK NQCC access program is progressing but has yet to produce a concrete result. Trimmed to fund this week's stronger NVIDIA and IonQ catalysts; also your largest AI-sleeve holding, so size this weight with that overlap in mind.

name: NVIDIA
note: NVIDIA's most active week in the sector in over a month: the new CUDA-Q Logical layer gave Fermilab a 7x development speedup, NVQLink ran its first live end-to-end quantum-GPU program with Quantum Machines (Sep 13), and NVentures reportedly joined QuEra's funding. Bumped up on the breadth of concrete, company-specific progress; also your largest cross-sector AI holding, so size for that concentration too.

name: IonQ
note: Recovered 6.5% to $39.13 on substance rather than guidance: a Best Paper win with Synopsys on quantum-accelerated CAE (14.6% faster execution) and the ORNL/NVIDIA DQAOA-GPT circuit-synthesis framework. Nudged up on the pivot from guidance-driven hype to peer-reviewed technical validation; still the cheapest pure-play on P/S (~64×).

name: Rigetti
note: DARPA formally confirmed Rigetti is not among the eleven companies in QBI Stage B, closing off a key optionality thesis flagged as pending in prior weeks. This week's 5.4% share gain rode broad sector sentiment, not company-specific news, so weight is trimmed toward the minimum while the CHIPS award and Purdue partnership keep this a Speculative rather than a Watch/Avoid.

name: Quantinuum
note: Shares are up 10.7% on top of last week's rally to a ~$14.3B market cap, while FY26 revenue guidance is unchanged at $28-32M — the valuation gap is widening faster than the (genuinely real) technical progress justifies. Trimmed toward the minimum: price has outrun fundamentals even though the underlying Helix/CHIPS story is intact. Also note the Aramco relationship overlaps with Microsoft's own AI-sleeve exposure.
